parts.passageHtml:
{[A.][209862]} {[In 1942 Allan R Holmberg, a doctoral student in anthropology from Yale University, USA, ventured deep into the jungle of Bolivian Amazonia and searched out an isolated band of Siriono Indians.][209863]} {[Siriono, Holmberg later wrote, led a "strikingly backward” existence.][209893]} {[Their villages were little more than clusters of thatched huts.][209902]} {[Life itself was a perpetual and punishing search for food: some families grew manioc and other starchy crops in small garden plots cleared from the forest, while other members of the tribe scoured the country for small game and promising fish holes.][209913]} {[When local resources became depleted, the tribe moved on.][209955]}

{[As for technology, Holmberg noted, the Siriono "may be classified among the most handicapped peoples of the world".][209966]} {[Other than bows, arrows and crude digging sticks, the only tools the Siriono seemed to possess were "two machetes worn to the size of pocket- knives".][209985]}

{[B.][210013]} {[Although the lives of the Siriono have changed in the intervening decades, the image of them as Stone Age relics has endured.][210015]} {[Indeed, in many respects the Siriono epitomize  the popular conception of life in Amazonia.][210038]} {[To casual observers, as well as to influential natural scientists and regional planners, the luxuriant forests of Amazonia seem ageless, unconquerable, a habitat totally hostile to human civilization.][210053]} {[The apparent simplicity of Indian ways of life has been judged an evolutionary adaptation to forest ecology, living proof that Amazonia could not - and cannot - sustain a more complex society.][210081]} {[Archaeological traces of far more elaborate cultures have been dismissed as the ruins of invaders from outside the region, abandoned to decay in the uncompromising tropical environment.][210110]}

{[C. The popular conception of Amazonia and its native residents would be enormously consequential if it were true.][210151]} {[But the human history of Amazonia in the past 11,000 years betrays that view as myth.][210169]} {[ Evidence gathered in recent years from anthropology and archaeology indicates that the region has supported a series of indigenous cultures for eleven thousand years; an extensive network of complex societies - some with populations perhaps as large as 100,000 - thrived there for more than 1,000 years before the arrival of Europeans.][210186]} {[(Indeed, some contemporary tribes, including the Siriono, still live among the earthworks of earlier cultures. )][210235]} {[Far from being evolutionarily retarded, prehistoric Amazonian people developed technologies and cultures that were advanced for their time.][210251]} {[If the lives of Indians today seem "primitive ", the appearance is not the result of some environmental adaptation or ecological barrier; rather it is a comparatively recent adaptation to centuries of economic and political pressure.][210270]} {[Investigators who argue otherwise have unwittingly projected the present onto the past.][210304]}

{[D. The evidence for a revised view of Amazonia will take many people by surprise.][210318]} {[Ecologists have assumed that tropical ecosystems were shaped entirely by natural forces and they have focused their research on habitats they believe have escaped human influence.][210332]} {[ But as the University of Florida ecologist, Peter Feinsinger, has noted, an approach that leaves people out of the equation is no longer tenable.][210359]} {[The archaeological evidence shows that the natural history of Amazonia is to a surprising extent tied to the activities of its prehistoric inhabitants.][210383]}

{[E. The realization comes too soon.][210407]} {[In June 1992 political and environmental leaders from across the world met in Rio de Janeiro to discuss how developing countries can advance their economies without destroying their natural resources.][210414]} {[The challenge is especially difficult in Amazonia.][210445]} {[Because the tropical forest has been depicted as ecologically unfit for large-scale human occupation, some environmentalists have opposed development of any kind.][210453]} {[Ironically, one major casualty of that extreme position has been the environment itself.][210476]} {[While policy makers struggle to define and implement appropriate legislation, development of the most destructive kind has continued apace over vast areas.][210490]}

{[F. The other major casualty of the "naturalism" of environmental scientists has been the indigenous Amazonians, whose habits of hunting, fishing, and slash-and-burn cultivation often have been represented as harmful to the habitat.][210514]} {[In the clash between environmentalists and developers, the Indians, whose presence is in fact crucial to the survival of the forest, have suffered the most.][210549]} {[The new understanding of the pre-history of Amazonia, however, points toward a middle ground.][210575]} {[Archaeology makes clear that with judicious management selected parts of the region could support more people than anyone thought before.][210589]} {[The long- buried past, it seems, offers hope for the future.][210610]}

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 1 - 3:

Choose the most suitable headings for sections A, B and D from the list of headings below.  Write the appropriate numbers i - vii in boxes 1 - 3 on your answer sheet.

List of Headings

i. Amazonia as unable to sustain complex societies

ii. The role of recent technology in ecological research in Amazonia

iii. The hostility of the indigenous population to North American influences

iv. Recent evidence

v. Early research among the Indian Amazons

vi. The influence of prehistoric inhabitants on Amazonian natural history

vii. The great difficulty of changing local attitudes and practices

Example

Answer

Paragraph C

iv

questions.explanationHtml:
1

Đoạn A (In 1942 Allan R Holmberg, a doctoral student in anthropology from Yale University, USA, ventured deep into the jungle of Bolivian Amazonia and searched out an isolated band of Siriono Indians. Siriono, Holmberg later wrote, led a "strikingly backward” existence.)

v

2

Đoạn B (To casual observers, as well as to influential natural scientists and regional planners, the luxuriant forests of Amazonia seem ageless, unconquerable, a habitat totally hostile to human civilization. The apparent simplicity of Indian ways of life has been judged an evolutionary adaptation to forest ecology, living proof that Amazonia could not - and cannot - sustain a more complex society.)

i

3

Đoạn D (The archaeological evidence shows that the natural history of Amazonia is to a surprising extent tied to the activities of its prehistoric inhabitants.)

vi (lịch sử tự nhiên của Amazon có gắn kết mật thiết “extent tied” với những cư dân tiền sử ở đây → có sự ảnh hưởng của cư dân tiền sử lên lịch sử tự nhiên của Amazon)

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 4 - 9:

Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage 2?

In boxes 4 - 9 on your answer sheet write

YES if the statement agrees with the views of the writer

NO if the statement contradicts the views of the writer

NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this

options.text: YES
NO
NOT GIVEN

questions.text: The reason for the simplicity of the Indian way of life is that Amazonia has always been unable to support a more complex society.
questions.explanationHtml:
4

Đoạn B (Archaeological traces of far more elaborate cultures have been dismissed as the ruins of invaders from outside the region, abandoned to decay in the uncompromising tropical environment.)

NO (lí do các nền văn hóa bị hủy hoại ở Amazon là do “invaders” - những kẻ xâm lược chứ không phải do Amazon không có khả năng hỗ trợ một xã hội phức tạp hơn → chỉ có lối sống đơn giản của người “Indian” ở đây )

questions.text: There are lessons to be learned from similar ecosystems in other parts of the world.
questions.explanationHtml:
6

Không có thông tin trong bài

NOT GIVEN

questions.text: There is a crucial popular misconception about the human history of Amazonia.
questions.explanationHtml:
5

Đoạn C (The popular conception of Amazonia and its native residents would be enormously

consequential if it were true. But the human history of Amazonia in the past 11,000 years betrays that view as myth.)

YES

questions.text: Most ecologists were aware that the areas of Amazonia they were working in had been shaped by human settlement.
questions.explanationHtml:
7

Đoạn D (Ecologists have assumed that tropical ecosystems were shaped entirely by natural forces and they have focused their research on habitats they believe have escaped human influence.)

NO (hệ thống rừng mưa nhiệt đới tại Amazon là được hình thành bởi thiên nhiên “natural forces” → TRÁI NGƯỢC ý của câu hỏi là do con người dựng nên “human settlement” 

 

Đây là ý kiến của “most ecologists” đa số các nhà sinh thái học là hệ thống nhiệt đới Amazon chỉ được tạo bởi thiên nhiên và trong đoạn D cũng đã có dẫn chứng chứng tỏ ý kiến này là SAI. Các bạn làm thêm các câu sau để hiểu nhé

questions.text: The indigenous Amazonian Indians are necessary to the well-being of the forest.
questions.explanationHtml:
8

Đoạn F (In the clash between environmentalists and developers, the Indians, whose presence is in fact crucial to the survival of the forest, have suffered the most.)

YES (paraphrase “crucial” thành “necessary” trong câu hỏi → sự tồn tại của cư dân Amazon rất quan trọng và cần thiết cho sự khỏe mạnh của các cánh rừng nơi đây)

questions.text: It would be possible for certain parts of Amazonia to support a higher population.
questions.explanationHtml:
9

Đoạn F (Archaeology makes clear that with judicious management selected parts of the region could support more people than anyone thought before.)

YES (“support more people” = “support higher population”)

Questions 10 - 13:

Choose the appropriate letters A-D and write them in boxes 10 - 13 on your answer sheet.

options.text: were unusually aggressive and cruel.
had had their way of life destroyed by invaders.
were an extremely primitive society.
had only recently made permanent settlements.

questions.explanationHtml:
10

Đoạn A (The Siriono, Holmberg later wrote, led a "strikingly backward” existence.)

C (“strikingly backward” nghĩa là trở về trước dòng thời gian một cách đáng kinh ngạc → đây là một bộ lạc cực kỳ tiền sử “primitive”)

options.text: are evidence of early indigenous communities.
are the remains of settlements by invaders.
are the ruins of communities established since the European invasions.
shows the region has only relatively recently been covered by forest.

questions.explanationHtml:
11

Đoạn C ( The popular conception of Amazonia and its native residents would be enormously consequential if it were true. But the human history of Amazonia in the past 11,000 years betrays that view as myth. Evidence gathered in recent years from anthropology and archaeology indicates that the region has supported a series of indigenous cultures for eleven thousand years; an extensive network of complex societies - some with populations perhaps as large as 100,000 - thrived there for more than 1,000 years before the arrival of Europeans.)

A (rất nhiều minh chứng cho thấy đã từng xuất hiện nhiều cộng đồng tiền sử bản địa ở Amazon)

options.text: has often been questioned by ecologists in the past.
has been shown to be incorrect by recent research.
was made by Peter Feinsinger and other ecologists.
has led to some fruitful discoveries.

questions.explanationHtml:
12

Đoạn D (The archaeological evidence shows that the natural history of Amazonia is to a surprising extent tied to the activities of its prehistoric inhabitants.)

B (hệ thống nhiệt đới ở Amazon không chỉ được tạo bởi thiên mà còn có mối quan hệ mật thiết với cư dân tiền sử của nó )

options.text: warn us against allowing any development at all.
cause further suffering to the Indian communities.
change present policies on development in the region.
reduce the amount of hunting, fishing, and ‘slash-and-burn’.

questions.explanationHtml:
13

Đoạn F (The new understanding of the pre-history of Amazonia, however, points toward a middle ground. Archaeology makes clear that with judicious management selected parts of the region could support more people than anyone thought before. The long- buried past, it seems, offers hope for the future.)

C (một vài nơi ở Amazon hoàn toàn có thể hỗ trợ một cộng đồng người rộng lớn hơn → sẽ có sự thay đổi trong chính sách phát triển nơi đây → cho cư dân nơi đây phát triển thành xã hội phức tạp vì họ rất là cần thiết cho sự tồn tại của khu rừng)
